topic: The Windmill Problem: A Dance of Geometry
target_audience: High school students and competitive math enthusiasts

sections.title: Introduction: Pip and the Star Field
lecture_lines: Imagine a star field with seven glowing points.
A robot, Pip, starts at pivot star A.
Pip holds a long, rotating laser beam.
The laser spins clockwise around the pivot point.
When it hits star B, the pivot will shift.
animations: Create a field of 7 white points (#FFFFFF) representing stars in a black background.
A point at the center turns yellow (#FFFF00) and is labeled 'A'.
A red line (#FF0000) appears, passing through 'A' at a 45-degree angle.
The red line rotates clockwise around 'A' at a constant speed.
As the line touches point 'B' (#FFFFFF), 'B' flashes cyan (#00FFFF) and the line stops.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Rotation and Pivot Points
lecture_lines: Avoid setups where three stars align.
We assume stars are in general position.
This ensures the laser hits only one at once.
animations: Show three points in a row with the red line (#FF0000) hitting all three; label 'Invalid' in red.
Show scattered points where the line hits only one at a time; label 'General Position' in white (#FFFFFF).
Animation of the line successfully pivoting from one point to exactly one other point.

sections.title: The Rule of the Windmill
lecture_lines: The laser always rotates clockwise around a pivot.
Striking a new star instantly transfers the center.
Rotation continues seamlessly around the new star.
animations: Red line (#FF0000) rotates clockwise around yellow pivot 'A' [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/windmill.svg].
Line hits point 'B' (#00FFFF); 'B' becomes yellow (#FFFF00) and 'A' turns white (#FFFFFF).
The rotation continues seamlessly around the new pivot 'B'.

sections.title: The Hidden Invariant: Counting Sides
lecture_lines: With seven points, one pivot leaves six others.
Three stars stay on each side of the laser.
As we pivot, the balance of points holds.
The old pivot enters the opposite side’s set.
Exactly three points always remain on each side.
animations: Set up 7 points: 1 yellow pivot, 3 blue points (#0000FF) on the left, 3 red points (#FF0000) on the right.
Start clockwise rotation; the line moves toward a red point.
Upon hitting a red point, the pivot transfers; the old pivot moves into the blue set.
The new pivot (previously red) is now 'on the line' and technically between sets.
Highlight that the count (3 on each side) remains constant throughout the process.

sections.title: The 180-Degree Flip
lecture_lines: Let’s rotate the laser by 180 degrees.
The progress bar tracks our total rotation.
Each star hit becomes a new pivot point.
After a half-turn, the line is parallel again.
This journey visits every single star in the field.
animations: Add a semi-circular progress bar at the bottom, initially empty.
Perform several windmill transitions (pivot swaps) using a laser [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/laser.svg] as the rotating line while the bar fills.
As each point is hit, mark it with a persistent gold circle (#FFD700).
The progress bar reaches 180 degrees; the line is now parallel to its starting position.
All 7 points are now marked with gold circles, showing all were visited.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Beauty of Combinatorial Geometry
lecture_lines: Simple invariants can explain complex geometric systems.
This is the famous 2011 IMO Windmill Problem.
Mathematical beauty emerges from these unchanging patterns.
animations: Display the complex 'web' formed by all the lines traced during the rotation.
Overlay text 'The Power of Invariants' and 'IMO 2011' in white (#FFFFFF).
Fade the scene into a single star field, leaving a sense of mathematical beauty.
